q: A student draws the cristae of a mitochondrion as separate, free-floating sacs inside the matrix. Why is this incorrect?
options: Cristae are folds of the inner membrane, so they must be drawn continuous with it
Cristae are part of the outer membrane, so they should be drawn attached to the outside
Cristae should be drawn as stacked, coin-like discs, in the same way as chloroplast grana
Cristae are found in the intermembrane space, not inside the matrix
explanation: The inner membrane folds inwards to form cristae, which project into the matrix; the space inside each fold connects to the intermembrane space. Free-floating sacs look like thylakoids – which in chloroplasts really are separate from the inner membrane. This is one of the most common reasons for losing a drawing mark.
